The 2024 New York's 26th congressional district special election was held on April 30, 2024, to fill the vacant seat in New York's 26th congressional district.[1] The seat became vacant after Democratic incumbent Brian Higgins resigned on February 2, 2024, to become president of Shea's Performing Arts Center.[2][3] The early voting period ran from April 20 to April 28, 2024.[4]

The Associated Press declared Tim Kennedy the winner within an hour of the polls closing.[5] He served in the United States House of Representatives for the remainder of the 118th United States Congress.

Nominees

[edit | edit source]

New York does not use primary elections when filling vacancies. Instead, party officials in the affected counties are responsible for choosing nominees.

Democratic Party

[edit | edit source]

The Erie County Democratic Committee chose their nominee on February 21, 2024.[6]

Candidates

[edit | edit source]
Nominated
[edit | edit source]
  • Tim Kennedy, state senator from the 63rd district (2011–present)[7]
Lost nomination
[edit | edit source]
  • Nate McMurray, former town supervisor of Grand Island and nominee for the 27th district in 2018 and 2020 (ran as an independent)[6]
  • Jeanne Vinal, Erie County legislator (2020–present)[7]
Declined
[edit | edit source]
  • Byron Brown, mayor of Buffalo (2006–2024), former chair of the New York Democratic Party (2016–2019), and former state senator from the 60th district (2001–2005)[8]
  • Mark Poloncarz, Erie County executive (2012–present)[9]

Republican Party

[edit | edit source]

The Erie County Republican Committee chose their nominee on February 21, 2024.[10]

Candidates

[edit | edit source]
Nominated
[edit | edit source]

Independents

[edit | edit source]

Withdrawn

[edit | edit source]
  • Nate McMurray,[b] former town supervisor[a] of Grand Island and nominee for the 27th district in 2018 and 2020[11]
